claims: Patriots' Day is observed on the third Monday in April.
Patriots' Day is observed on April 20, 2026.
Patriots' Day is a civic holiday in Massachusetts and Maine.
Patriots' Day commemorates the opening battles of the American Revolutionary War at Lexington and Concord in 1775.
Patriots' Day commemorates the "shot heard 'round the world" on April 19, 1775.
The "shot heard 'round the world" on April 19, 1775 marks the start of the Revolutionary War.
The Boston Marathon is traditionally held on Patriots' Day Monday.
The Boston Marathon runs from Hopkinton to Boston.
Battle reenactments on Patriots' Day are held in Lexington at Battle Green.
Battle reenactments on Patriots' Day are held in Concord at North Bridge.
State offices in Massachusetts are closed on Patriots' Day Monday.
Municipal offices in Massachusetts are closed on Patriots' Day Monday.
Schools in Massachusetts are closed on Patriots' Day Monday.
Some businesses in Massachusetts are closed on Patriots' Day Monday.
There is a parade in Lexington on Patriots' Day.
There are ceremonies at Minute Man National Historical Park on Patriots' Day.
There is a Boston Red Sox home game on Patriots' Day.
The 2016 film Patriots Day was directed by Peter Berg.
The 2016 film Patriots Day centers on the 2013 Boston Marathon bombing.
The 2016 film Patriots Day centers on the days-long manhunt for the terrorists.
Mark Wahlberg plays Sgt. Tommy Saunders in the 2016 film Patriots Day.
Kevin Bacon plays FBI Agent Richard DesLauriers in the 2016 film Patriots Day.
John Goodman plays Comm. Ed Davis in the 2016 film Patriots Day.
J.K. Simmons plays Sgt. Jeffrey Pugliese in the 2016 film Patriots Day.
Michelle Monaghan plays Carol Saunders in the 2016 film Patriots Day.
The 2016 film Patriots Day was produced by Scott Stuber, Mark Wahlberg, Hutch Parker, Dylan Clark, Stephen Levinson, Peter Berg, and Michael Radutzky.
Patriots' Day 2026 events span from April 17 to April 21, 2026.
State services close on Patriots' Day.
The U.S. Postal Service remains open on Patriots' Day.
